title: Sorted Squares and K-th Smallest Square
prompt:
### Part 1

Implement `sorted_squares(nums) -> list[int]` for an integer array sorted in nondecreasing order. Return its squares in nondecreasing order in `O(n)` time, without calling a sorting operation. Preserve duplicates and do not mutate the input. Empty input returns `[]`.

### Part 2

Implement `kth_smallest_square(nums, k) -> int`, with one-based `k` and `1 <= k <= len(nums)`. Target `O(log n + k)` time and `O(1)` auxiliary space: locate the split between negative and nonnegative values, then merge outward by magnitude until the k-th value. Do not build all sorted squares.

Practice reconstruction: one-based rank, valid-input assumptions, and follow-up complexity are explicit conventions. Emitting `k` values from the two outer endpoints yields the k-th largest square, so that source suggestion must be adapted for the smallest-square follow-up.
